phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Rate-limiting for sidecar requests (blob sidecars and data column sidecars) IS implemented in the Prysm beacon chain codebase. The implementation uses a leaky bucket algorithm with per-peer, per-topic rate limiters. The rate-limiting spans multiple abstraction layers: request validation, quota tracking, and batch throttling.

state_anomalies_found.description: The bucketMap type (map[string]*LeakyBucket) can grow unbounded as new peer keys are added. While PeriodicPrune() removes empty buckets, high-volume attack scenarios could create many non-empty buckets simultaneously.

abstract_state.growth_pattern: monotonic increase bounded by peer count and pruning frequency
abstract_state.max_theoretical_size: unbounded (limited by number of unique peer IDs)
abstract_state.actual_constraint: pruned every c.period (1 second or 30 seconds depending on topic)

potential_consequences: Memory exhaustion under sustained attack from many unique peers
Lock contention on Collector.lock during high-concurrency scenarios
mitigation_observations: PeriodicPrune() runs concurrently to remove empty buckets
Peer scoring system (downscorePeer) can eventually ban misbehaving peers
Initial heap capacity is pre-allocated to 4096 entries to reduce reallocations

state_anomalies_found.description: The validateRequest function treats amt=0 as amt=1 ('Treat each request as a minimum of 1'), but this normalization happens AFTER checking if amt > remaining. A request with amt=0 against an exhausted bucket (remaining=0) would pass the check (0 > 0 is false), then get normalized to 1 after validation succeeds.

abstract_state.transformation: if amt == 0 then amt := 1 (but only after validation)

potential_consequences: Edge case where zero-amount requests could bypass rate limit check
Unlikely to be exploitable since actual RPC handlers pass non-zero totalRequested values
mitigation_observations: Actual handlers like dataColumnSidecarByRootRPCHandler compute totalRequested before calling validateRequest
The normalization comment suggests this is intentional for empty requests
Stream is still charged via rateLimiter.add() after the response is sent

state_anomalies_found.description: The Count() method uses now() to compute remaining capacity by calculating time-based decay. Multiple calls to Count() within the same request flow could return different values due to time progression, potentially causing TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) inconsistencies.
potential_consequences: Between validateRequest() and add(), bucket count could decrease, allowing slightly over-limit requests
Race is bounded by request processing time (typically microseconds to milliseconds)
mitigation_observations: Collector uses a mutex (sync.RWMutex) to protect concurrent access
Time window is small (< request processing time)
Over-limit is bounded by natural time decay, not attacker-controlled

state_anomalies_found.description: The totalRequested counter is computed as a sum of len(ident.Columns) across all identifiers. With a malicious payload containing many identifiers with large column sets, totalRequested could theoretically overflow, but this is checked against MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars before use.

abstract_state.computation: sum of len(ident.Columns) for all ident in requestedColumnIdents

potential_consequences: If MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars is sufficiently large and len(requestedColumnIdents) is large, integer overflow is theoretically possible before validation
In practice, network message size limits prevent this
mitigation_observations: P2P encoding layer has message size limits that bound len(requestedColumnIdents)
Validation occurs before rate limiter is charged

state_anomalies_found.description: The batch throttling uses a ticker that delays every batchSize items. The ticker is created ONLY if len(requestedColumnIdents) > batchSize, meaning requests at or below batchSize are processed without throttling, regardless of their actual item count.

abstract_state.initialization: if len(requestedColumnIdents) > batchSize then time.NewTicker(tickerDelay) else nil
abstract_state.usage: delays processing after every batchSize columns

potential_consequences: A request with len(requestedColumnIdents) <= batchSize but sum(len(ident.Columns)) > batchSize could process more items without throttling
This is by design but creates a throttling granularity boundary
mitigation_observations: Rate limiter still enforces per-second limits via leaky bucket
Ticker throttling is a secondary, batch-level control
The condition len(requestedColumnIdents) > batchSize vs totalRequested > batchSize is semantically different

rate_limiter_architecture.implementation: Leaky Bucket Algorithm (as meter, not queue)

enforcement_points.action: collector.Add(peer, amt) - charges peer's bucket after successful response

dataColumnSidecarByRootRPCHandler: 2. Compute totalRequested = sum(len(ident.Columns)) for all idents
5a. If count % batchSize == 0 and ticker != nil: wait for ticker.C
5c. Retrieve and send data column sidecars
leaky_bucket_count_computation: 1. If now() >= bucket.p: bucket is empty, return 0
3. nsPerDrip = period / rate (nanoseconds per token leak)

trust_boundary_verification.boundary: P2P network peer -> Beacon node RPC handler
trust_boundary_verification.rate_limiting_layer: Applied at RPC handler entry point (before request processing)
trust_boundary_verification.per_peer_isolation: YES - buckets are keyed by peer ID (stream.Conn().RemotePeer().String())
trust_boundary_verification.topic_isolation: YES - separate collectors for different RPC topics
trust_boundary_verification.global_limit: NO - limits are per-peer, not global (could be enhanced with global collector)

attack_resistance.sybil_attack: PARTIAL - limited by peer scoring and connection limits (not analyzed in this scope)
attack_resistance.slowloris: MITIGATED - per-peer rate limits prevent single peer from monopolizing resources
attack_resistance.burst_attack: MITIGATED - burst factor allows temporary spikes but enforces long-term rate
attack_resistance.distributed_attack: PARTIAL - each peer limited independently, but many peers can saturate collectively

prysm_changelog_evidence: Line 228: 'Ensures the rate limitation is respected for by root blob and data column sidecars requests. [[PR]](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/15981)'

phase1_abstract_interpretation.conclusion: The audit item's initial assessment that 'No specific rate-limiting code found' is INCORRECT. Comprehensive rate-limiting IS implemented for sidecar requests using a per-peer, per-topic leaky bucket algorithm. The implementation includes request validation, quota enforcement, peer downscoring on violations, and batch throttling. Several low-severity edge cases exist (ALAT-001 through ALAT-005) but do not constitute critical vulnerabilities. The trust boundary integrity is maintained through multi-layered rate limiting.
